full_text_en:
Guangdong Zhitong Telecom Co., Ltd. v. Hong Fenming — Telephone Fee Dispute

Plaintiff (Counterclaim Defendant): Guangdong Zhitong Telecom Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. Tangxin West Street, Xinshi, Guangzhou City.

Legal Representative: Zhou Changbin, General Manager of the Company.

Agents ad litem: Liang Junchi and Xie Hong, lawyers from Guangdong Xinchengli Law Firm.

Defendant (Counterclaim Plaintiff): Hong Fenming, male, 57 years old. Domicile: Xiaogang Heng Street, Guangzhou City.

Plaintiff Guangdong Zhitong Telecom Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Zhitong Company") filed a lawsuit with the Haizhu District People's Court of Guangzhou City against defendant Hong Fenming over a telephone fee dispute.

The plaintiff alleged: The defendant made calls using two mobile phone numbers activated upon his application with our company, but failed to pay the call fees from June 1998. The plaintiff requested the court to order the defendant to pay the overdue call fees and late fees totaling RMB 8,055.87.

The defendant answered and filed a counterclaim: I initially paid over RMB 6,000 in network access fees to the plaintiff and activated two mobile phone numbers in my name from the plaintiff. These two numbers have become my private property. Since I am not the actual user of these two numbers, I was unaware that call fees were overdue. After these numbers fell into arrears, the plaintiff never notified me, as the owner, so that I could handle the matter promptly; nor did they suspend service in accordance with their regulations, intentionally allowing the loss from call fees to continue to expand. Therefore, I do not agree with the plaintiff's claims. Furthermore, without my knowledge, the plaintiff sold these two numbers to others on the grounds that I owed call fees. This action both damages my reputation and infringes upon my property rights. I request the court to order the plaintiff to compensate me for the network access fees for the two numbers, compensate me for reputational damage, and bear all costs of this case.

The plaintiff answered the counterclaim: Our company suspended service for these two mobile phones on July 26, 1998, so there is no issue of loss expansion. Since the defendant still did not pay the call fees and late fees within three months after suspension, our company transferred these two mobile phone numbers to others in accordance with the agreement between the parties, which is completely lawful and reasonable. We disagree with the defendant's counterclaim.

The Haizhu District People's Court of Guangzhou City found through trial:

On January 12, 1998, the defendant, Hong Fenming, applied for and activated two mobile phone numbers, namely 1382546588 and 1382546598, at the plaintiff Zhitong Company by filling out the "Guangzhou Digital Mobile Phone (GSM) Installation Application Card" and signing a "Mobile Phone User Agreement" with Zhitong Company. The above two mobile phone numbers did not pay the call fees for June 1998 on time. On July 26 of the same year, Zhitong Company suspended service for the two mobile phone numbers. By October of the same year, the cumulative overdue call fees and late fees for 1382546588 totaled RMB 3,328.36, and for 1382546598 totaled RMB 4,727.61. In November of the same year, Zhitong Company transferred these two mobile phone numbers to others.

It was further found: Article 10 of the User Instructions on the "Guangzhou Digital Mobile Phone (GSM) Installation Application Card" states: "After three months of suspension, this business office has the right to transfer the user's number to others for use, and all network access fees will not be refunded."

The above facts are confirmed by documentary evidence such as the "Guangzhou Digital Mobile Phone (GSM) Installation Application Card" and the "Mobile Phone User Agreement," as well as the statements of both parties.

The Haizhu District People's Court of Guangzhou City held: The defendant, Hong Fenming, became a mobile phone user of Zhitong Company by signing an agreement with the plaintiff, Zhitong Company. Zhitong Company activated two mobile phone numbers for Hong Fenming as agreed, fulfilling its obligations. Hong Fenming should, in accordance with the agreement, perform the obligation to pay fees on time after using these two mobile phone numbers to make calls. Hong Fenming failed to pay the call fees for June for a period of five months and should bear fault liability. Zhitong Company's request for Hong Fenming to pay the call fees and late fees is lawful and reasonable and should be supported. Timely payment is an obligation undertaken by the mobile phone user under the agreement, and Zhitong Company did not need to give separate notice. Hong Fenming's claim that Zhitong Company did not formally notify him to pay the call fees lacks sufficient evidence and is not upheld. Zhitong Company's transfer of the phone numbers to others after three months of suspension without payment by the mobile phone user, in accordance with the agreement, was not improper. Hong Fenming's claim that this action caused him reputational and property damage lacks sufficient evidence and is not upheld. Pursuant to Article 111 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "If a party fails to perform its contractual obligations or performs them in a manner that does not conform to the agreed terms, the other party has the right to demand performance or take remedial measures and has the right to claim compensation for losses," the Haizhu District People's Court of Guangzhou City hereby adjudges:

1. The defendant, Hong Fenming, shall pay the plaintiff, Zhitong Company, mobile phone call fees and late fees totaling RMB 8,055.97 within 15 days from the effective date of this judgment.

2. The counterclaim of the defendant, Hong Fenming, is dismissed.

After the first-instance judgment was announced, the defendant, Hong Fenming, appealed, alleging: The appellee, Zhitong Company, failed to suspend service for three consecutive months when the user did not pay call fees on time, which involves an element of deception. Zhitong Company, without notifying the owner, privately transferred the phone numbers to others, infringing upon the appellant's property rights. The appellant requested that the mobile phone network access fees paid by the appellant be used to offset the overdue call fees, with the appellant paying only the shortfall, or paying only 50% of the call fees.

The appellee, Zhitong Company, answered in agreement with the first-instance judgment.

During the second-instance trial at the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court, the appellee, Zhitong Company, indicated willingness to refund the network access fees to the appellant at the current mobile phone network access price.

The Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court held through trial:

The facts found in the first-instance judgment are clear and the evidence is sufficient. After the appellee, Zhitong Company, discovered that the appellant, Hong Fenming, had failed to pay the June call fees, it suspended service for Hong Fenming's two mobile phone numbers in July in accordance with regulations. Hong Fenming's appeal claim that Zhitong Company failed to suspend service for three consecutive months after discovering the overdue call fees, causing loss expansion, was merely a misunderstanding of the timing of billing and payment by the telecom department, and he did not submit evidence to support this assertion; therefore, it is not upheld.

The mobile phone communication channel represented by a mobile phone number is a resource developed by the mobile phone company. By charging users mobile phone network access fees, the mobile phone company transfers the right to use this resource to the user. By paying the network access fee, the user purchases the right to use a certain channel. Although this channel remains under the control of the mobile phone company, it has become a resource available for the user to use at any time. When the user uses this channel to make calls, the mobile phone company provides the call service and is naturally entitled to charge the user call fees. Network access fees and call fees are two different types of fees set for different transaction purposes and cannot be conflated. When a user owes call fees, the mobile phone company, to protect its own interests, has the right to take measures to prohibit the user from making calls (i.e., suspend service), and also has the right to demand payment of the overdue call fees and additional late fees. However, it cannot, on the grounds that the user owes call fees, take advantage of its control over the mobile phone channel to reclaim the channel that has been paid for by the user without compensation, and even transfer it to others for use. Article 10 of the User Instructions on the "Guangzhou Digital Mobile Phone (GSM) Installation Application Card" of the appellee, Zhitong Company, which states "After three months of suspension, this business office has the right to transfer the user's number to others for use, and all network access fees will not be refunded," appears as a standard term clause that emphasizes only its own rights, neglects the user's interests, infringes upon the property rights of the appellant, Hong Fenming, and violates the principle of fairness. This standard term clause should be declared invalid. Zhitong Company shall bear corresponding civil liability for the transfer of Hong Fenming's phone numbers. The grounds for Hong Fenming's counterclaim in the first instance and this part of the appeal in the second instance are valid and should be supported. Considering that Hong Fenming's two mobile phone numbers have been used for some time, and the current mobile phone network access fee has dropped to RMB 1,020 per number, Zhitong Company expressed willingness during the second-instance trial to refund the network access fees to Hong Fenming at the current price. If Zhitong Company refunds the network access fees at this price, it can ensure that Hong Fenming enjoys the right to use the two mobile phone numbers. Therefore, this expression of intent by Zhitong Company should be permitted. The first-instance judgment was erroneous in its determination of the validity of Zhitong Company's transfer of Hong Fenming's mobile phone numbers and should be corrected. Accordingly, the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, hereby adjudges:

1. The first item of the first-instance civil judgment is affirmed;

2. The second item of the first-instance civil judgment is vacated;

3. The appellee, Zhitong Company, shall, within 15 days from the date of receipt of this judgment, refund to the appellant, Hong Fenming, the network access fees for the two mobile phone numbers totaling RMB 2,040.
